title: docs: update DreamShaper Vast fleet
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Replaces retired DreamShaper instance `46387155` with RTX 4070 instance `47789794` in the fleet inventory.
- Records machine `100803`, the `$0.093889/hour` all-in rate, and the new named tunnel hostname.
- Updates the DreamShaper server table for the mixed RTX 3090/4070 pool.
- Uses the refactored `operations/infrastructure/gpu/dreamshaper/` model path.

Validation:
- `git diff --check`
- Candidate restart and public-path image tests passed.
- Post-cutover sample: 39 successful renders, 3 intentional queue spills, 0 backend errors.

gist.headline: DreamShaper gets fresh wings
gist.blurb: A retired DreamShaper worker has made way for a new RTX 4070 in the rendering garden. The hive kept producing pixels through the handoff, as hives tend to do when the paperwork is good.
gist.summary: DreamShaper’s fleet inventory now records RTX 4070 machine 100803 replacing retired instance 46387155, with the mixed RTX 3090/4070 server pool and new tunnel hostname documented under the refactored dreamshaper path.
gist.impact: DreamShaper image generation now has a documented RTX 4070 backend in its mixed fleet, with cutover validation reporting 39 successful renders and no backend errors.
gist.visual_concept: Depict DreamShaper as a cozy pixel-art image workshop where Polli welcomes a new RTX 4070-powered retro computer into a garden of rendering machines. A small server rack with a lime-green route/tunnel cable and pixel flowers represents the refreshed backend fleet; Polli’s mechanic accessory makes her part of the upgrade rather than a bystander.
gist.image_prompt: Cozy pixel art scene in a warm garden-server shed where the cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings wears a tiny mechanic tool belt while connecting a lime green (#ecf874) cable to a friendly retro GPU computer labeled “RTX 4070”; nearby code-plants bloom beside older RTX 3090 terminals. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike, with subtle CRT glow and a warm cream background.
